title: A New Era for Digital Twins: Progress and Industry Adoption
content: This systematic review examines recent advancements in Digital Twin (DT) technology and its transformative impact across multiple sectors. A Digital Twin is a real-time digital replica of a physical system that integrates monitoring, simulation, and optimization to enhance efficiency, resilience, and sustainability. DT systems rely on sensors, data acquisition networks, and computational infrastructure for real-time data processing. Machine learning and analytics provide predictive capabilities, while edge computing and communication protocols ensure rapid, secure data exchange. High-resolution imaging, visualization tools, and scanning technologies improve modeling precision. Blockchain and cybersecurity frameworks protect data integrity, and advanced databases with feedback mechanisms enable continuous system refinement. DTs support predictive maintenance, workflow optimization, and rapid prototyping, contributing to lower operational costs. In healthcare, DTs enable personalized diagnostics and treatment plans, while in urban planning and infrastructure, they help design smarter, sustainable environments. Energy systems benefit from operational optimization and renewable integration. DTs also enhance training through immersive simulations and improve the reliability of autonomous systems and supply chains. Industries such as manufacturing, aerospace, automotive, oil and gas, transportation, and marine engineering increasingly depend on DTs to boost performance and mitigate risk. This review presents current DT implementations and identifies key research areas to advance, scale, and secure next-generation DT technologies.
